name: zt-idea-grow
description: Grow the ZET Topic trees from a finished Literature tree, as Luhmann wrote his main-box Cards from his bibliographic notes: DeepSeek reads each section of the Literature tree against the whole box and keeps the core, related, useful, interesting and intuitive ideas as standalone Topic-tree Cards filed beside the Cards they continue; zt-digest grow checks, writes, fixes and reports the Topic share
whenToUse: After a digest (zt-econ-digest, zt-math-digest) has built a book's Literature tree, or for any Literature tree in either Workspace: give the Citation key and a fresh work folder. Writes only agent Topic trees. Not for building a Literature tree.

preflight.P1: Goal and result: the reader's own ideas from one Literature tree, written as agent Topic-tree Cards (docs/idea-grow-design.md; the Topic proposals P1-P7 of docs/topic-tree-ideas-proposals.md live here, not in the digests). Result: the grow stage's plan line, rounds, report line (Cards, Topics, same, refused, duplicates, faults left, Topic share before and after) and the cleaned workspaces; grow-report.md in the work folder.
preflight.P2: Inputs: book (Citation key, required), out (the work folder, required; also the DeepSeek workspace), from/to (an optional section range: at most 120 sections per run), fixRounds (0-2, default 1), dshModel (default the official DeepSeek V4.1 Flash source, deepseek-official/deepseek-flash: the user wants the official source only), effort (high or max; never lower).
preflight.P3: Units of work: first one Topic-planning job over the whole book (gt-001: the sections' anchors and the Topic catalogue; it reuses agent Topics and opens at most max(2, ceil(sections/2)) <= 8 new ones), then one section per DeepSeek job: an anchor of the Literature tree (Key/n) with its subtree. zt-digest grow -Step plan writes gt-001 and the section files; -Step topics makes the run's Topics and writes jobs\gw-NNN.md with them; each step prints only counts, and the module names the jobs gw-001..gw-N. Fix jobs are one per section with faults (fxR-NNN), from -Step check's count.
preflight.P4: Roles: runner (Haiku, low) relays each zt-digest grow command and returns its last line; DSMP managers (Haiku, fixed by the protocol) run up to 8 DeepSeek conversations each, at most 8 at once, approve only the read-only helper, the precheck, reads under the work folder and JSON writes under out, and delete every conversation. DeepSeek (official source, high effort, skills zettelkasten and asd-ste100-zh) writes only its answer file. No Sonnet or Opus role: scripts plan, check and write.
preflight.P5: Stage graph: grow (one module stage: plan -> DeepSeek topic plan -> topics -> DeepSeek ideas -> apply -> links -> DeepSeek link jobs -> apply -> check/fix rounds -> report -> cleanup) -> report (value). The rounds are sequential inside the module because each apply needs every answer of its round, and the section jobs need the run's Topics.
preflight.P6: Modules: zt-grow-cycle v3 (project folder scripts/idea-grow/workflow/modules; requires the framework's script, deepseek and the DSMP block) and value. The prompt template is scripts/idea-grow/dsh-grow-instructions.zh.md, read by -Step plan from disk.
preflight.P7: Checks: every DeepSeek job runs its SELF-CHECK (zt-digest grow -Step precheck: G1-G10, with Link kinds read as zt reads them, and zt-check on the drafts; the topic job: ids, existing agent roots, near names, sections, the bound) until faults: 0, and its answer must end OK or FLAG; apply validates every answer again and refuses each idea with a fault; check runs zt-check --cards with the book on every Card the run wrote and turns each hard fault into a fix job; the grow stage expects a report.
preflight.P8: Failure policy, modes, checkpoints: grow retries 0 (a rerun with the same out resumes: applied sections are skipped, their answers kept) and halts; report always runs after grow. No modes, no checkpoints. The DeepSeek cleanup runs in a finally block.
preflight.P9: Dry run and pilot: zt-idea-grow.sim.json stands in for plan (2 sections), the topic manager, topics (2 jobs), one manager, apply, check (one fix), report and cleanup. Pilot 1 (1.0.0, 2026-10-20): 8 sections of grossman2002integration, 53 Topic Cards, Topic share 1.6% -> 47.4%, 0 faults left, but 8 new Topics (4 on one concept) and every related idea branched off the one earlier Topic Card; 1.1.0 plans the run's Topics first, appends a root-direct idea to the main line, and reads Link kinds as zt does (G10). Pilot 2 (1.1.0): 4 run Topics (3 new, 379/0 reused), 58 Topic Cards, 0 faults, share 49.6%, 5 min; but the main-line append joined five parallel sections into one blind 20-step chain in 389. 1.2.0: a later root placement opens a line beside the doorway (n/1|a …), and the section chains its ideas in it. Pilot 3 (1.2.0): 4 run Topics, 56 Topic Cards, each Topic a doorway with one line per section (391/1|a..f), 0 faults, share 48.7%; but only 6 of 56 Cards linked another Topic tree, all to the one earlier Card 379/1. 1.3.0 adds the link round: one DeepSeek job per Topic tree the run wrote in (gl-NNN), Links to Cards of other trees, at most 2 per Card, each one sentence with its kind (G11), appended to the Card. Pilot: the Literature tree of grossman2002integration (trial 13's digest groups) in a fresh folder, e.g. {book: 'grossman2002integration', out: 'D:\\zt-grow\\grossman2002integration-pilot'}; back up the archive first.

runner.description: relays one zt-digest grow command and returns its last stdout line

book.description: the Citation key of the Literature tree to grow from

out.description: the work folder: plan files, answers, state, report; also the DeepSeek workspace

from.description: the first section (anchor number) to grow

to.description: the last section (anchor number) to grow

fixRounds.description: fix rounds after the first apply

dshModel.description: the DeepSeek Harness model (the official source)

stages.title: Grow
stages.detail: plan the sections, DeepSeek keeps the ideas, write the Topic Cards, check, fix, report, clean up

expect.message: the grow stage wrote no report
